Subject: Acme POC - Next steps and success criteria (recap)

Hi Alex / Priya — great conversation earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before we kick off the trial/POC:

Scope recap:
- Evaluate Redwood inference runtime for Acme's customer support summarization pipeline (multilingual, ~500 reqs/min peak).
- Focus on latency, summary fidelity, and hallucination reduction compared to current pipeline.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm / edit):
1) Latency: 95th percentile tail latency < 450ms for 512-token requests in our dedicated test harness.
2) Quality: ROUGE-L improvement >= 8 points vs baseline on curated test set + human grade >= 4/5 on semantic correctness.
3) Hallucination: <2% critical hallucinations on spot checks (examples attached).
4) Cost: token cost per summary <= 0.20 USD (projected) or clear path to meet within 30% of target with batching/quantization.

Eval plan (high level):
- Offline eval (week 1): run curated test set through Redwood and baseline; automated metrics + human grading using the attached evaluation template (acme-poc-eval-template.xlsx).
- Shadow/online eval (week 2–3): low-traffic shadow of live requests with logging and A/B telemetry; collect latency + user acceptance metrics.
- Final review (end of week 3): alignment call to review results and sign off on next phase.

Ownership / ask:
- Acme: provide sample corpus + 200 annotated examples for human grading by 11/24.
- Redwood: set up dedicated trial environment, baseline run, and initial offline eval by 11/27.
- Owners: Alex (Acme) – data + access; Priya (Acme) – PO and timeline; Marissa (Redwood) – SE lead for evals; Dylan (Redwood) – commercial lead.

Attachments: acme-poc-eval-template.xlsx (evaluation template) and a draft SOW (will share in follow-up).

Next steps: please confirm the success criteria and the owner assignments by end of day Monday (11/23). If that looks good we will schedule the kickoff for Wed 11/25 (30–45 min).

Thanks,
Dylan

Subject: Re: Acme POC - Eval plan & success criteria (methodology + rubric)

Hi Alex / Priya — thanks for the quick replies. Per Dylan's recap, below is a proposed eval methodology and a simple grading rubric we plan to use during the offline phase. I also call out the trade-offs between an offline-only approach and running a short shadow phase.

1) Offline eval (what we run first)
- Purpose: verify model correctness and establish measurable deltas vs baseline before any live traffic exposure.
- Inputs: curated test set (provided by Acme) + 200 human-annotated examples for semantic correctness.
- Metrics we will compute programmatically: ROUGE-L, BLEU, token-length distributions, latency (p50/p95/p99), and hallucination proxy (entity-contradiction rate).
- Human grading: each example gets 3 human raters; scoring rubric below. We will aggregate median score and compute inter-rater agreement.

2) Shadow/online eval (recommended after offline pass)
- Purpose: validate behavior on live distribution, capture operational metrics (real latency, memory/kv cache behavior), and collect click/acceptance signals if available.
- Mode: traffic mirrored (non-retroactive) to Redwood trial instance, return results to internal logs but not to end-users.
- Duration: 7–14 days at low traffic (1–5% of baseline traffic) depending on signal volume.

3) Grading rubric (human) — per-example score 1–5:
- 5 (Excellent): Accurate, concise, preserves intent, no hallucinations. Ready for production with minor or no edits.
- 4 (Good): Minor factual issues or omissions; requires small edit.
- 3 (Acceptable): Usable but needs a moderate edit; not risky.
- 2 (Poor): Significant inaccuracies or misleading content; not acceptable for production.
- 1 (Fail): Dangerous/inaccurate/hallucinated output.

Aggregations and thresholds (proposal):
- Median human grade >= 4.0 across evaluation set.
- >= 90% of examples grade >= 3.
- Hallucination (critical) < 2% on spot-checks.
- Latency: p95 < 450ms; p99 < 900ms (report both).

4) Practical notes / reproducibility
- We'll provide an evaluation notebook and the grading spreadsheet (see attached template). Please keep test-set versions immutable during the run.
- For offline runs we will seed the workload and keep the same prompts/temperature settings as the shadow run to ensure comparability.

5) Ownership and deliverables
- Acme: deliver curated test set + 200 annotated examples by 11/24; designate a technical contact for data access.
- Redwood (Marissa): run offline eval, produce a results deck with per-metric breakdown by 11/27.
- Redwood (Dylan): commercial checkpoint and summary for execs by end of POC.

If this looks good I will create the eval job and share the notebook + rubric link. Happy to hop on a 30-min call to walk through the scoring process.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
